builder_plan.scenario: An agent looks good in demos, but you cannot tell which product tasks it fails.
builder_plan.change: Use the study's evaluation idea to inspect a small set of tasks with human-checked answers.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current evaluator and a manually reviewed reference set.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Agreement with human review, missed failures, false alarms, and evaluation cost per task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: VeriCUA: Verification as Agentic Exploration for Computer-Using Agents
summary: VeriCUA replaces single-pass VLM trajectory judges and generated state-inspection programs with a rubric-driven verifier that dynamically selects GUI or code checks and fuses evidence under explicit rules, usable across platforms without per-platform verifier engineering. The cost is additional inference and interaction: each verification episode requires context inspection, exploratory GUI or code actions, and evidence aggregation, raising latency and API or GPU spend per judgment relative to a single VLM call. It can fail when decisive evidence is unreachable through either GUI or code access, when the constructed rubric omits a task requirement, or when exploration itself perturbs application state in online settings.
rationale: For a small team evaluating or curating data for computer-using agents on constrained infrastructure, a platform-agnostic verifier built on existing VLM APIs is feasible to pilot, but its unquantified accuracy gains and added per-judgment cost require validation on the reader's own environments before replacing simpler judges.

claims.statement: VeriCUA replaces single-pass VLM trajectory judges and generated state-inspection programs with a rubric-driven verifier that dynamically selects GUI or code checks and fuses evidence under explicit rules, usable across platforms without per-platform verifier engineering. The cost is additional inference and interaction: each verification episode requires context inspection, exploratory GUI or code actions, and evidence aggregation, raising latency and API or GPU spend per judgment relative to a single VLM call. It can fail when decisive evidence is unreachable through either GUI or code access, when the constructed rubric omits a task requirement, or when exploration itself perturbs application state in online settings.

Improved agreement with reference labels over VLM-judge and program-generation baselines across online and offline settings, with the largest offline gains on hard cases and stronger rejection of false completion claims online; no numeric magnitude is given in the abstract.
